current_example.title: Example: Finding a Joint Probability for Some Independent Random Variables Using Marginal PDFs

q-143344.name: Question 1
q-143344.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}({x}^{2}+1), & \,0\le x\le 1, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}y, & \,0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the joint probability density function $f(x,y).$
q-143344.worked_solution:
Two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability density functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}({x}^{2}+1)\cdot \frac{1}{2}y \\  & =\frac{3}{8}({x}^{2}+1)y\end{aligned}
$$

where $(x,y)\in [0,1]\times [0,2].$ Therefore, the full expression for $f(x,y)$ is

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{8}({x}^{2}+1)y, & \,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let X and Y be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

fX(x)={34(x2+1),0≤x≤1,0,otherwisefY(y)={12y,0≤y≤2,0,otherwise

Find the joint probability density function f(x,y).

a
 f(x,y)={14(x2+1)y,0≤x≤1,0≤y≤20,otherwise
b
 f(x,y)={38x2(y+1),0≤x≤1,0≤y≤20,otherwise
c
 f(x,y)={18x(y2+1),0≤x≤1,0≤y≤20,otherwise
d
f(x,y)={38(x2+1)y,0≤x≤1,0≤y≤20,otherwise
e
 Impossible to determine using only the given information.
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Two continuous random variables X and Y with joint probability density function f(x,y) are independent if and only if

f(x,y)=fX(x)⋅fY(y)

for all possible values x and y, where fX(x) and fY(y) are the marginal probability density functions for X and Y, respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

f(x,y)=fX(x)⋅fY(y)=34(x2+1)⋅12y=38(x2+1)y

where (x,y)∈[0,1]×[0,2]. Therefore, the full expression for f(x,y) is

f(x,y)={38(x2+1)y,0≤x≤1,0≤y≤20,otherwise

q-143346.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}\,{x}^{3}, & \,0\le x\le 2, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}(y+2), & \,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the joint probability density function $f(x,y).$

*Hint: We do not know if $X$ and $Y$ are independent.*
q-143346.worked_solution: Since we don't know whether $X$ and $Y$ are independent, it is impossible to determine the joint distribution of $X$ and $Y$ using only the given information.

q-143349.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}(x-1), & \,2\le x\le 3, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{e}^{y}, & \,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the joint probability density function $f(x,y).$

*Hint: We do not know if $X$ and $Y$ are independent.*

q-143349.knowledge_point: Finding the Joint PDF of Two Independent Random Variables Using Marginal PDFs

q-143348.name: Question 4
q-143348.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}, & \,1\le x\le 2, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}4{y}^{3}, & \,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the joint probability density function $f(x,y).$
q-143348.worked_solution:
Two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability density functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}\cdot 4{y}^{3} \\  & =\frac{8{y}^{3}}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

where $(x,y)\in [1,2]\times [0,1].$ Therefore, the full expression for $f(x,y)$ is

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{8{y}^{3}}{{x}^{2}}, & \,1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let X and Y be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

fX(x)={2x2,1≤x≤2,0,otherwisefY(y)={4y3,0≤y≤1,0,otherwise

Find the joint probability density function f(x,y).

a
 f(x,y)={y34x2,1≤x≤2,0≤y≤10,otherwise
b
f(x,y)={8y3x2,1≤x≤2,0≤y≤10,otherwise
c
 f(x,y)={8x3y2,1≤x≤2,0≤y≤10,otherwise
d
 f(x,y)={y38x2,1≤x≤2,0≤y≤10,otherwise
e
 Impossible to determine using only the given information.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Two continuous random variables X and Y with joint probability density function f(x,y) are independent if and only if

f(x,y)=fX(x)⋅fY(y)

for all possible values x and y, where fX(x) and fY(y) are the marginal probability density functions for X and Y, respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

f(x,y)=fX(x)⋅fY(y)=2x2⋅4y3=8y3x2

where (x,y)∈[1,2]×[0,1]. Therefore, the full expression for f(x,y) is

f(x,y)={8y3x2,1≤x≤2,0≤y≤10,otherwise

q-143350.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x, & \,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2}, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}5{y}^{4}, & \,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the joint probability density function $f(x,y).$

q-143370.name: Question 6
q-143370.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}(x+1), & \,0\le x\le 2, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{y}, & \,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X\le 1,Y\le 1).$
q-143370.worked_solution:
Two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability density functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(x+1)\cdot \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{y} \\  & =\frac{3}{8}(x+1)\sqrt{y},\end{aligned}
$$

where $(x,y)\in [0,2]\times [0,1].$ Therefore, the full expression for $f(x,y)$ is

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{8}(x+1)\sqrt{y}, & \,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 1,Y\le 1) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{8}(x+1)\sqrt{y}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3(x+1)}{8}{[\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{{y}^{3}}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{4}(x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}+\frac{x}{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{4})-0 \\  & =\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-143354.name: Question 7
q-143354.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{9}x, & \,0\le x\le 3, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡y, & \,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{2}, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X\le 2,Y\le 3).$
q-143354.worked_solution:
Two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability density functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =\frac{2}{9}x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡y \\  & =\frac{2}{9}x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

where $(x,y)\in [0,3]\times [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].$ Therefore, the full expression for $f(x,y)$ is

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{9}x\operatorname{sin}⁡y, & \,0\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{2} \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2,Y\le 3) & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{2}{9}x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{2}{9}x[-\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{0}^{\pi /2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{2}{9}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{(2)^{2}}{9}-0 \\  & =\frac{4}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-143353.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2x}, & \,0\le x, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}y, & \,1\le y\le 3, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X\le 1,Y\le 2).$
q-143353.worked_solution:
Two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability density functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =2{e}^{-2x}\cdot \frac{1}{4}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}y{e}^{-2x},\end{aligned}
$$

where $(x,y)\in [0,\infty )\times [1,3].$ Therefore, the full expression for $f(x,y)$ is

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}y{e}^{-2x}, & \,0\le x,\,1\le y\le 3 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 1,Y\le 2) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{2}y{e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-2x}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{4}{e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{3{e}^{-2x}}{8}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{3{e}^{-2}}{8}-(-\frac{3}{8}) \\  & =\frac{3}{8}(1-\frac{1}{{e}^{2}}).\end{aligned}
$$
